title: Fabric and Texture Basics
summary: Students learn beginner-friendly English for fabric names, textile observation, texture, surface, weight, movement, opacity, comfort, and fabric use so they can describe a swatch and connect material choice to garment type and design purpose.
essential_question: How can I describe what a fabric is like and what it is good for in simple English?
professional_context: Week 7 connects English to introductory sewing, early textile study, garment planning, and design decision-making. Students move from describing how a look appears visually to describing what a garment is made of, how a fabric feels and looks, how it behaves, and what it can be used for.
language_focus: fabric, textile, material, swatch, and sample words
common fabrics such as cotton, denim, linen, silk, wool, polyester, lace, and leather
texture and surface adjectives such as soft, rough, smooth, shiny, and matte
weight, movement, structure, and visibility words such as lightweight, heavy, stretchy, stiff, flowy, structured, transparent, and opaque
grammar_focus: The jacket is made of denim.
using feels for touch and texture
using good for for garment use and weather use
using fabric names as simple material nouns such as This is cotton and This is denim
teacher_preparation: Preview the Week 7 opener board, the common-materials board, the texture-and-qualities board, the reading gallery, and the reusable four-swatch gallery before class.
Prepare visible sentence frames for This is ..., It is made of ..., It feels ..., It looks ..., It is good for ..., It can be used for ..., and I like this fabric because ....
Keep the main writing task line-based and scaffolded. Do not turn the Fabric Swatch Description Card into a paragraph or word-count assignment.
Review likely Week 7 correction targets such as missing of in made of, confusion between feels and looks, and adjective order in phrases such as a soft cotton fabric and a heavy denim jacket.
Decide whether students will use a projected gallery, printed swatch cards, or physical fabric samples alongside the future app-style gallery for the teacher session.
Keep the Week 7 listening audio or teacher read-aloud fallback aligned to the same image A to D gallery used in listening, writing, and speaking.
student_deliverables: Completion of the Week 7 opener selections.
Completion of the main common-materials matching set.
Completion of the main texture-and-qualities matching set.
Reading-comprehension responses matching three swatch descriptions to image A, image B, or image C and answering detail questions.
Listening-comprehension responses identifying four fabrics from one audio clip.
Completion of made of, feels, looks, and good for phrase-practice frames.
A scaffolded Fabric Swatch Description Card with 6 required sentence-frame lines and 1 optional challenge sentence.
One corrected Week 7 sentence saved after review.
A short teacher-observed oral fabric description using prepared sentence frames.
